notes.why: A saturated yellow-to-pink-to-violet gradient fills the whole field. A soft glossy blob, a centered bold headline and three rounded cards on one axis give it a friendly hierarchy that reads in seconds.
notes.avoid: Do not copy the generic gradient-plus-emoji-card template. The emoji icons and identical frosted cards look stock and give the brand no distinct identity.
notes.keep: Keep the single glossy 3D blob above the headline. It gives the page one focal object and sets a playful tone with no extra decoration.

notes.why: A clear hierarchy of bold left-aligned headline, a single product-frame placeholder, a logo row and three equal feature cards keeps the page calm and easy to scan on a white ground.
notes.avoid: Do not copy the generic SaaS template of empty browser mockup, pale grey-blue palette and interchangeable card trio, because nothing about it is distinctive or memorable.
notes.keep: Keep the tight, bold sans headline paired with small colored uppercase category labels on the cards, which gives a quick scanning system at very little visual cost.

notes.why: Oversized slab-serif glyphs in neon yellow and magenta sit scattered on a near-black field, and thin hairline rules plus tiny monospace labels give them a strict structure to play against.
notes.avoid: Do not copy the large empty areas and the very small meta text, because they leave the lower half dead and the labels hard to read.
notes.keep: Keep the scale contrast between huge specimen letters and tiny mono captions, held together by a hairline-ruled stat and nav grid in two accent colors.

notes.why: A strict column grid, hairline rules and one tight bold grotesk headline over small gray metadata rows give a clear hierarchy with almost no ornament.
notes.avoid: Do not copy the generic white-on-black-text minimalism without real content rigor, because the system only works when the index rows and column alignment are precise.
notes.keep: Keep the numbered index table with hairline dividers, where each row aligns project name, category and sector to fixed columns.

notes.why: One oversized black grotesk wordmark sits centered on a warm off-white field, and tiny corner meta text frames it, so the eye has one place to go.
notes.avoid: Do not copy the empty space without the scale contrast, because a small wordmark in this much space looks unfinished instead of confident.
notes.keep: Keep the single full-width heavy wordmark, paired with a tiny two-line descriptor and small corner navigation labels.

notes.why: A near-black ground, one large serif headline with a single gold italic phrase, and small spaced-caps metadata create a clear hierarchy with a lot of empty space.
notes.avoid: Do not copy the empty gray placeholder cards, which look unfinished, or the very small low-contrast gray body and meta text, which is hard to read.
notes.keep: Use one accent color and one italic style on a few words of a large white serif headline, with everything else kept quiet.

notes.why: A cream ground, one serif family and a narrow centered column give the page a calm, print-like rhythm. Thin hairline rules and a small tracked eyebrow set the hierarchy without adding color or weight.
notes.avoid: The striped placeholder block stands in for real imagery, so copying it would make the feature card look empty and unfinished.
notes.keep: Keep the large centered serif headline, with a tiny uppercase eyebrow above it and a hairline rule below, on the warm cream ground.

notes.why: A saturated red-orange field, a huge black grotesk headline and hard-ruled index rows give a strict hierarchy, and the black and yellow blocks add contrast without breaking the grid.
notes.avoid: Do not copy the tiny low-contrast orange body text on the black card, because it is hard to read and weakens the loud tone.
notes.keep: Keep the oversized black heavy-grotesk headline on a single flat saturated ground, with one outlined letter 'O' as the only playful move.
